target_customer: Mobile engineering and security teams at banks, fintechs, healthtech and e-commerce companies
problem: Mobile apps are attacked at runtime through tampering, hooking, API abuse and AI-powered fraud, and protecting them normally needs SDK integration and code changes.
business_model: B2B security platform; protections applied to compiled APK or IPA builds with no SDK; pricing not published

founders.name: Kareem Selim
founders.background_notes: YC bio says he used to break apps for a living; launch post says he and the CTO have 15 combined years in offensive security.

founders.name: Hassan Mostafa
founders.background_notes: Spent years breaking apps for banks and fintechs per YC page. The founders have known each other 10 years and won CTFs and hackathons together.

competitors.name: Appdome
competitors.what: No-code mobile app protection injected in CI/CD
competitors.traction_then: the established no-code option in 2026 roundups

competitors.name: Guardsquare
competitors.what: DexGuard and iXGuard obfuscation plus RASP
competitors.traction_then: called the depth leader by reviewers

competitors.name: Promon
competitors.what: RASP-first app shielding popular in banking

competitors.name: RAVEN.IO
competitors.what: Runtime security platform stopping app exploits

technical_complexity.rationale: Binary-level instrumentation of compiled Android and iOS apps that detects hooking, tampering and emulators without SDKs requires deep reverse engineering expertise.

defensibility.rationale: Offensive security know-how and per-app protections are hard to copy quickly, but Appdome, Guardsquare and Promon already sell similar protections to banks.

market_need_then: Banks and fintechs face rising mobile fraud and compliance pressure (OWASP MASVS, PCI DSS). The founders cite 16 customers and 25 apps in third party profile (yespress); company site claims 20M+ end users protected.

branding.domain_note: Uses raspire.com exact match; no purchase story found.

identity.visual_style: Pragmatic B2B security site with stats
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and absolute, for example Security that works every time your app does; short fragments.

branding.brand_signature: No SDKs, no code changes, no release friction
branding.community_and_virality: Covered by MENA startup press when it joined YC (menastartupdigest, Arab Founders); no community evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: The name plausibly blends RASP and aspire, which is my inference since no source explains it; it is easily confused with Aspire brands in search.

outcome_analysis: Raspire is a Cairo-based Spring 2026 YC company selling no-code mobile runtime security, founded by two offensive security practitioners. It is too early for an outcome. It reports early customers in banking and fintech, but must prove it can displace established shielding vendors.
notes: Funding conflicts: yespress says about $505K from 500 Global, Sanabil 500 and Plus VC (March 2026), another founder profile says a $130,000 seed in 2026-03, Briter says undisclosed. No primary announcement, so no round recorded. YC team size shown as 3 on one page and 5 on another. Outcome search returned nothing relevant (name confusion with Careem). Education and prior employers not found.
